proposals.before: Volume 64b, Part Two: biographies of Yan An, Zhu Mai Chen, Wuqiu Shouwang, Zhufu Yan, Xu Le, Yan Cang, Zhong Jun, Wang Bao, and Jia Yi—the thirty-third set of biographies, lower scroll.
proposals.after: Volume 64b, Part Two: biographies of Yan An, Zhu Mai Chen, Wuqiu Shouwang, Zhufu Yan, Xu Le, Yan An, Zhong Jun, Wang Bao, and Jia Juanzhi—the thirty-third set of biographies, lower scroll.
proposals.reason: The second 嚴 in the surname-title list is not a distinct Yan Cang (no 蒼 in the Chinese), and 賈 in this Hanshu chapter is Jia Juanzhi rather than Jia Yi; the English invents given names absent from the Chinese title.

proposals.before: Qin then sent Commandant Tuo leading troops to garrison Yue.
proposals.after: Qin then sent Commandant Zhao Tuo leading troops to garrison Yue.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic correctly identifies 尉佗 as Commandant Zhao Tuo; the literal should retain the surname Zhao.

proposals.before: Now wild beasts share horns—brightness is the same root.
proposals.after: Now wild beasts share a joined horn—clearly showing they are of the same root.
proposals.reason: 明同本也 means the omen clearly shows a shared root; the literal misreads 明 as brightness.

proposals.before: When six wild geese beat their way upwind, the Spring and Autumn Annals read it as ill omen.
proposals.after: When six wild geese beat their way upwind, it is read as contrary/ill omen.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names no book here; the idiomatic invents an explicit Spring and Autumn Annals attribution.

proposals.after: Jun replied to the throne, saying:
proposals.reason: 軍上對曰 is a reply submitted upward to the emperor; the literal omits the 上對 sense.

proposals.before: Hand that smith the rough ingot of a Gan Jiang blade, let him quench the edge in pure water and true the guard on a Yue whetstone, and the finished sword will slice dragons in the river and rhinoceros hide on land as easily as a comet streaks or a brush draws a line in wet plaster.
proposals.after: Have a skilled smith cast the rough blank of a Gan Jiang blade, quench its edge in pure water and true its guard on a Yue whetstone, and the finished sword will slice dragons in the river and rhinoceros hide on land as easily as a comet streaks or a brush draws a line in wet plaster.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English opens with ungrammatical 'Hand that smith' and underplays the sense of a skilled smith casting the Gan Jiang blank.

proposals.before: Yi Yin labored over pots and chopping boards; the Grand Duke was reduced to working as a butcher; Baili Xi sold himself, and Ning Qi fed oxen. In this way they escaped their hardships.
proposals.after: Yi Yin labored over pots and chopping boards; the Grand Duke was reduced to working as a butcher; Baili Xi sold himself, and Ning Qi fed oxen. In this way they suffered these hardships.
proposals.reason: In 離此患也, 離 means to encounter/suffer (as 罹); the worthies endured these hardships, they did not escape them.

proposals.before: Thus Yi Yin labored at cauldrons and chopping boards, the Grand Duke was reduced to wielding a butcher's knife, Baili Xi sold himself, and Ning Qi fed oxen; thereby they escaped these hardships.
proposals.after: Thus Yi Yin labored at cauldrons and chopping boards, the Grand Duke was reduced to wielding a butcher's knife, Baili Xi sold himself, and Ning Qi fed oxen; thereby they suffered these hardships.
proposals.reason: Same error as the idiomatic line: 離此患也 is suffer/encounter these hardships, not escape them.

proposals.before: If obtaining intent is thus, then what barbarian prohibition does not stop, what command does not go?
proposals.after: If obtaining intent is thus, then what prohibition does not stop, what command does not go?
proposals.reason: Here 胡 is the interrogative 'how/what', not the ethnonym 'barbarian'.

proposals.before: Following and roaming the tendency of nature, in the field of quiet plain non-action, auspicious signs arrive of themselves, long life has no border, harmonious ease with folded hands, forever ten thousand years—why must one bend and stretch and twist trust like Pengzu, exhale and inhale like Qiao and Song, subtly cut off custom and leave the world!
proposals.after: Following and roaming the tendency of nature, in the field of quiet plain non-action, auspicious signs arrive of themselves, long life has no border, harmonious ease with folded hands, forever ten thousand years—why must one bend and stretch like Pengzu, exhale and inhale like Qiao and Song, subtly cut off custom and leave the world!
proposals.reason: 詘信 is the binome 屈伸 (bend and stretch); rendering 信 as 'trust' is a semantic error.

proposals.before: The emperor ordered Bao and Zhang Ziqiao and others together to await edict; repeatedly followed Bao and others on release hunts; at favored palaces and lodges, then composed songs and eulogies, ranked their high and low, and by gradation granted silk.
proposals.after: The emperor ordered Bao and Zhang Ziqiao and others together to await edict; repeatedly took Bao and others along on hunts; at favored palaces and lodges, then composed songs and eulogies, ranked their high and low, and by gradation granted silk.
proposals.reason: 數從褒等放獵 means the emperor had Bao and the others accompany him on hunts; 從 is not 'followed Bao'.

proposals.before: In decline, kings marched south and never came home; Duke Huan of Qi had to rescue the house of Zhou, and Confucius set the record straight in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
proposals.after: In decline, kings marched south and never came home; Duke Huan of Qi had to rescue the house of Zhou, and Confucius fixed its text.
proposals.reason: The Chinese only has 孔子定其文; naming the Spring and Autumn Annals is an unsupported invention in the idiomatic English.

proposals.before: Yang Xing said, 'The emperor once said that I was better than Grandee Xue. It should be easy for you to help me.
proposals.after: Xing said: 'The county office [His Majesty] once said Xing was better than Grandee Xue; I am easy to help.
proposals.reason: The literal field duplicates the idiomatic English instead of rendering 縣官嘗言興瘉薛大夫，我易助也.

proposals.before: Your servant foolishly thinks that what are not cap-and-girdle states, what the Tribute of Yu reaches, what the Spring and Autumn governs—all may for the moment be left undone.
proposals.after: Your servant foolishly thinks that those that are not cap-and-girdle states within the reach of the Tribute of Yu and the governance of the Spring and Autumn may for the moment all be left alone.
proposals.reason: The literal treats 禹貢所及 and 春秋所治 as separate parallel categories to leave undone, obscuring that they delimit the civilized sphere contrasted with 非冠帶之國.

proposals.before: Thereupon an edict was issued, saying: 'Zhuya captives killed clerks and people, turned their backs and rebelled as traitors; now those who court discuss say some may strike, some may guard, some wish to abandon them—their aims each differ.
proposals.after: Thereupon an edict was issued, saying: 'Zhuya's rebels killed clerks and people, turned their backs and rebelled as traitors; now those discussing at court say some may strike, some may guard, some wish to abandon them—their aims each differ.
proposals.reason: 珠崖虜殺 means Zhuya rebels killed officials, not 'captives killed'; 廷議者 means court discussants, not 'those who court discuss.'

proposals.before: Even ancestral offerings are curtailed in years of famine; how can I court the shame of chasing a pointless slight to the ends of the earth?
proposals.after: Even ancestral-temple sacrifices are incomplete in famine years; how much less should I shrink from a humiliation that is not truly shameful?
proposals.reason: 況乎辟不嫌之辱 means declining a shame that is not a real disgrace (不嫌), not 'chasing a pointless slight.'

proposals.before: The document says: "Slanderous talk and extinguished conduct alarm Our hosts."
proposals.after: The Documents say: "Slanderous talk and extinguished conduct alarm Our hosts."
proposals.reason: 書曰 cites the classic Documents (Shangshu); singular 'document' understates the titled source.

proposals.before: The world calls Gongsun Hong having excluded Zhufu, Zhang Tang having trapped Yan Zhu, Shi Xian having slandered Juanzhi; inspecting their tracks and conduct, Zhufu sought the eminence of the minister's tripod and obtained clan execution; Yan and Jia passed in and out of the forbidden gate summoning power and profit—their deaths were each their proper lot—what resentment then about exclusion and entrapment!
proposals.after: The world says Gongsun Hong excluded Zhufu, Zhang Tang trapped Yan Zhu, and Shi Xian slandered Juanzhi; inspecting their tracks and conduct, Zhufu sought the eminence of the minister's tripod and obtained clan execution; Yan and Jia passed in and out of the forbidden gate summoning power and profit—their deaths were each their proper lot—what resentment then about exclusion and entrapment!
proposals.reason: English grammar is broken ('calls Gongsun Hong having excluded'); needs finite verbs to match Chinese 世稱…排/陷/譖.

decisions.after: Volume 64b, Part Two: biographies of Yan Zhu, Zhu Mai Chen, Wuqiu Shouwang, Zhufu Yan, Xu Le, Yan An, Zhong Jun, Wang Bao, and Jia Juanzhi—the thirty-third set of biographies, lower scroll.
decisions.reason: s0001’s title 嚴朱吾丘主父徐嚴終王賈傳 lists only surnames; the first 嚴 is Yan Zhu (嚴助) and the second 嚴 is Yan An (嚴安), while 賈 is Jia Juanzhi (賈捐之). The before invents Yan Cang and Jia Yi; the proposed after wrongly makes both 嚴 into Yan An.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 嚴朱吾丘主父徐嚴終王賈傳

decisions.reason: s0032 has only 尉佗; the literal “Commandant Tuo” matches the Chinese. Adding Zhao supplies a surname absent from this unit (identification already present in the idiomatic).

sourceWitness.excerpt: 秦乃使尉佗將卒以戍越

decisions.reason: In 今野獸并角，明同本也, 明 is adverbial “clearly,” not “brightness,” and 并角 is a joined horn; the proposed literal corrects both misreadings.

decisions.after: When six wild geese beat their way upwind, it is read as a contrary omen.
decisions.reason: s0077 蓋六鶂退飛，逆也 names no book; inventing the Spring and Autumn Annals is unsupported. The proposed slash “contrary/ill” is unnatural, so the wording is tightened while keeping 逆.
軍上對曰 is adequately rendered by “Jun submitted a reply”; 上對’s upward submission is already in “submitted,” and “replied to the throne” is only a stylistic clarification.
s0153 巧冶鑄干將之樸 needs a grammatical English opening for the skilled smith casting the Gan Jiang blank; “Hand that smith” is ungrammatical and the proposed repair restores the sense.
In 離此患也, 離 is 罹 “suffer/encounter”; the preceding hardships are what the worthies underwent, not what they escaped, and the replacement is accurate.
The same 離此患也 on the literal line means suffer these hardships, not escape them; the proposed fix is correct.
In 則胡禁不止，曷令不行, 胡 is interrogative in parallel with 曷, not the ethnonym “barbarian”; removing that gloss is required.
詘信 is the binome 屈伸 “bend and stretch”; reading 信 as “trust” is a semantic error, and the proposed deletion fixes it.
數從褒等放獵 has the emperor take Bao and the others along on hunts; “followed Bao” reverses the accompaniment relation expressed by 從.
s0221 has only 孔子定其文; the idiomatic’s “Spring and Autumn Annals” is an unsupported addition, and “fixed its text” matches the Chinese.

decisions.after: Xing said: 'The emperor once said Xing was better than Grandee Xue; I am easy to help.
decisions.reason: s0268 興曰：「縣官嘗言興瘉薛大夫，我易助也」 uses Xing (not “I”) as the compared person and ends “I am easy to help.” The before errs on both points; the proposed “county office [His Majesty]” is an awkward calque—縣官 here is the emperor.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 縣官嘗言興瘉薛大夫，我易助也

decisions.after: Your servant foolishly thinks that those that are not cap-and-girdle states, that the Tribute of Yu does not reach, and that the Spring and Autumn does not govern, may for the moment all be left alone.
decisions.reason: 非 scopes over 冠帶之國、禹貢所及、春秋所治: lands outside the cap-and-girdle realm and outside Yu Gong / Spring and Autumn geography. The before treats the last two as positive categories to abandon; the proposed after wrongly keeps them inside the civilized sphere.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 非冠帶之國，禹貢所及，春秋所治，皆可且無以為

decisions.reason: 珠崖虜殺吏民 means Zhuya’s rebels/caitiffs killed officials and people, and 廷議者 are those discussing at court; “captives” and “those who court discuss” are mistranslations.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 珠崖虜殺吏民……今廷議者

decisions.after: Even ancestral-temple sacrifices are incomplete in famine years; how much more should one avoid a humiliation that is not truly shameful?
decisions.reason: 況乎辟不嫌之辱哉 follows the famine-sacrifice a fortiori: 辟 is avoid/set aside, and 不嫌之辱 is a disgrace that is not real shame. The before invents “chasing a pointless slight”; the proposed “how much less should I shrink from” garbles 況乎 and 辟.
書曰 is the standard citation formula for the Documents (Shangshu); singular “document” understates that titled classic, and the idiomatic already reads “Documents.”
世稱公孫弘排主父，張湯陷嚴助，石顯譖捐之 needs finite verbs; “calls Gongsun Hong having excluded” is broken English, and the proposed repair matches the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 世稱公孫弘排主父，張湯陷嚴助，石顯譖捐之

claimRetractions.reason: Attestation dates for p006 presuppose a distinct Yan Cang; the title supports no such person or interval.

claimRetractions.reason: The BC 200–169 interval is Jia Yi’s lifespan, supplied only because the bad translation took 賈 as Jia Yi; s0001’s title gives no such dates for Jia Juanzhi.

claimRevisions.reason: Revised r0011 restores 賈 in this chapter title as Jia Juanzhi (賈捐之), not Jia Yi (賈誼); the personal-name claim must follow the chapter’s biographee.

claimAdditions.reason: The corrected title names the same Jia Juanzhi whose biography explicitly begins at Emperor Yuan's accession in 48 BC, providing the required attested time marker.
